issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: For physical abuse by a romantic partner, the threat profile is centered on generalized danger from strangers, while the appraisals are centered on bodily damage/shame and permanent emotional change. This is not impossible, but as the only represented components it is clinically hard to integrate into a single coherent profile of partner abuse without any partner-specific or trauma-linked threat content.

issues.item: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: Within the formulation, the only active links are between Negative Appraisals and Threat, so these two nodes should strongly cohere. Here the negative appraisals imply consequences focused on the body and self after intimate physical abuse, but the threat item 'threat from strangers approaching me' points to a different danger representation that is not reflected in the appraisals. That weakens the expected tight appraisal-threat coupling.

vignette: Mary is an 80-year-old woman from Oceania who has been experiencing significant psychological distress following a history of physical abuse by her romantic partner. Her trauma has left deep scars, both physically and emotionally, and she now finds herself in a constant state of vigilance and fear. The abuse Mary experienced was relentless and severe, often leaving her with bruises and injuries that took weeks to heal. Over time, these experiences have led her to develop a profound sense of physical vulnerability. She has come to believe that her body has been permanently damaged by what happened, making it difficult for her to trust its resilience and strength anymore. This deep-seated belief that she is physically vulnerable has created an unrelenting fear within her. Mary's negative appraisals about her own body and emotions have become a central part of her daily life. She feels certain that she will never be able to feel normal emotions again, which has left her feeling disconnected from the world around her. The trauma has also led her to believe that she can no longer trust her own body-a sentiment that compounds her feelings of vulnerability. These negative appraisals have significantly contributed to Mary's heightened sense of threat. She often finds herself waking up in the middle of the night, unable to shake off the feeling that something might be wrong. Even inside her own home, where she once felt safe, she now feels on guard at all times. Her fear is so intense that it disrupts her sleep and makes it difficult for her to relax. Mary's occupation as a welder has also been affected by these experiences. The constant vigilance and the fear of being hurt again have made it challenging for her to focus fully on her work. She often feels on edge, particularly when she is in close proximity to others, which can be especially difficult given the collaborative nature of welding. Mary's husband has noticed a change in her behavior over time. He sees how she checks every corner and door before going to bed, and he worries about how much she struggles with sleep. Despite his efforts to reassure her, Mary cannot shake off the belief that something bad could happen at any moment. This ongoing threat perception further reinforces her negative appraisals, creating a vicious cycle of fear and distrust. Mary's negative appraisals have become deeply intertwined with her sense of threat. She has come to believe that her body is unreliable and that she will never feel normal again, which only exacerbates her constant state of alertness. The more she feels threatened, the more she questions her physical integrity and emotional stability, perpetuating a cycle of fear and doubt. Mary finally decided to seek help after a particularly frightening night when she woke up in the middle of the dark, her heart racing with anxiety. She realized that these fears were no longer just fleeting thoughts but had become a constant presence in her life. What frightens her most is the idea of living with this fear indefinitely and being unable to reclaim any sense of normalcy or trust. Mary hopes that by seeking help, she can regain some control over her emotions and physical sensations. She wants to be able to sleep without waking up in panic and to feel safe within her own home again. Most importantly, Mary is hoping for a future where she no longer feels the constant threat looming over her life and can begin to trust herself and her body once more.
